academic_translation:
Flies, gadflies, and bees,
And likewise whatever has become a worm—
Even they, if they generate the power of diligence,
Will attain unsurpassable awakening, which is hard to attain.
translation: Think of flies, gadflies, bees, and worms. If even they build up the power of joyful effort, they will reach the highest awakening, which is very hard to achieve.

academic_translation:
"But my arms, legs, and so forth,
Must be given away, so I am afraid," if I think—
Without analyzing what is heavy and what is light,
I am merely afraid due to delusion.
translation: I might think, "I am afraid to give away my arms and legs." But this fear is just confusion. I am not weighing what matters more and what matters less.

academic_translation:
Because this bodhisattva, through the power of bodhicitta,
Exhausts previous misdeeds
And gathers an ocean of merit,
He is explained to be superior to the Śrāvakas.
translation: The power of the awakening mind uses up past harmful deeds. It also gathers an ocean of stored goodness. Because of this, the bodhisattva is greater than the Hearers.

academic_translation:
The good qualities of myself and others,
Which are many, I must accomplish;
Wherein if for each and every good quality
I must familiarize myself for an ocean of eons,
translation: I must build up many good qualities in myself and others. If I must practice each and every good quality for an ocean of great ages,

academic_translation:
Because I have been devoid of aspiration for the Dharma,
Previously and even now,
Such destitution has come about;
Who would forsake aspiration for the Dharma?
translation: Because I did not have a strong wish for the teachings in the past, and still do not have it now, I have ended up in such a sad, empty state. Who would ever give up a strong wish for the teachings?

academic_translation:
Habituated to that in another life,
Misdeeds and suffering will increase.
Another deed, and the time of the result,
Will become inferior, and that other deed too will not be accomplished.
translation: If I get used to giving up, it will happen in another life too. My harmful deeds and suffering will increase. Any other action, and the time of its result, will become weak. Then that other action will not get finished either.

academic_translation:
Karma, afflictions, and capacity:
One should cultivate pride in these three.
Thinking, "I shall do it alone,"
This is pride in action.
translation: I should build my pride in three things: my action, my power over troubling emotions, and my ability. Thinking, "I will do this alone," is pride in action.

academic_translation:
If one is not satiated by sensual desires,
Which are like honey smeared on a razor's edge,
By merit, whose ripening is happiness and which is peaceful,
How could one ever be satiated?
translation: If we never get enough of our desires for pleasure, which are like honey smeared on a razor's edge, how could I ever get enough of a store of goodness? Its ripening is happiness and peace.

academic_translation:
Just as a veteran warrior, together with enemies,
Clashes swords on the battlefield,
One should dodge the weapons of the afflictions
And strike to destroy the enemy afflictions.
translation: Just like an experienced warrior clashing swords with enemies on a battlefield, I must dodge the weapons of the troubling emotions. Then I must strike to destroy those enemy troubling emotions.

academic_translation: From Entering the Way of the Bodhisattva, this is the seventh chapter, entitled the Exposition of Diligence.

locked_terms.use: Entering the Way of the Awakening Hero

translation: From Entering the Way of the Awakening Hero, this is the seventh chapter, called the Teaching on Joyful Effort.

academic_translation:
If they are not seen, one feels no joy,
And the mind does not rest in meditative equipoise;
Even when they are seen, one is not satisfied,
And is tormented by craving just as before.
translation: If we do not see them, we feel no joy, and the mind cannot become a settled mind. Even when we do see them, we are never satisfied. We are still hurt by wanting, just as before.

academic_translation:
If one shares the same fortune as a childish one,
One will certainly go to the lower realm;
If they lead one to a fortune unlike that of the noble ones,
What is the use of relying on a childish one?
translation: If I share the same fate as a childish person, I will certainly go to an unhappy realm. If they lead me to a fate unlike that of the noble ones, what is the use of relying on a childish person?

academic_translation:
If one associates with a childish one, from that childish one,
Self-praise, the disparagement of others,
And talk that delights in saṃsāra and so forth—
Non-virtue will certainly arise in every way.
translation: If I spend time with a childish person, bad deeds will definitely happen. That childish person brings about praising oneself and putting others down. We will talk about enjoying the cycle of rebirth and things like that.

academic_translation:
Thus, when oneself and another rely on each other,
By that, one will merely come to ruin;
Since they do not accomplish my welfare,
And I too will not accomplish their welfare,
translation: Because they will not do me any good, and I will not do them any good either, we will only ruin ourselves.

academic_translation:
Just as a bee takes nectar from a flower,
Having taken only what serves the purpose of the Dharma,
As if I had never seen them before,
I shall remain without familiarity toward everyone.
translation: A bee just takes nectar from a flower. In the same way, I will only take what helps me practice the teachings. I will not become close to anyone, as if I had never seen them before.

academic_translation:
Since sentient beings have diverse aspirations,
if even the Victors cannot please them,
what need is there to mention an inferior one like me?
Therefore, I shall abandon thoughts of the world.
translation: Living beings have many different strong wishes. If even the Victorious Ones cannot please them all, how could someone as lowly as me do it? Therefore, I will let go of my thoughts about the world.
In the past, you sent many messengers and made many requests for their sake. You did not hesitate to do harmful deeds or ruin your good name for them.

academic_translation:
That which you first lifted with effort,
and though drawn up, looked down out of modesty;
whether seen before or unseen,
that face was covered by a cloth.
translation: At first you worked hard to lift that face. Even when you lifted it up, it looked down shyly. Whether you had seen it before or not, that face was covered by a cloth.

academic_translation:
You yourself contain much impurity,
Which you constantly make use of;
And yet for other bags of filth as well,
You desire them out of greed for impurity.
translation: You are full of filth yourself. You use it all the time. Yet you still want other bags of filth. You desire them out of greed for filth.

academic_translation:
Not only do you not disparage
Your own impurity,
But out of greed for impurity,
You also desire another bag of filth.
translation: You do not even look down on your own filth. But out of greed for filth, you also desire another bag of filth.

academic_translation:
If, by merely a ten-millionth fraction of that
Hardship, Buddhahood is accomplished,
For a lustful person, compared to the conduct of awakening,
The suffering is greater, yet there is no awakening.
translation: Even a ten-millionth part of that hardship could bring us to the state of a Buddha. A person full of desire goes through greater suffering than the way of acting for awakening. Yet they get no awakening at all.

academic_translation:
Acting independently and without attachment,
Unconnected to anyone at all,
Whatever happiness of contentment one enjoys,
That is difficult even for Indra to find.
translation: They act on their own without clinging and are not tied to anyone at all. The joy of being happy with enough is hard even for Indra to find.

academic_translation:
I should dispel the suffering of others
Because it is suffering, like my own suffering.
I should benefit others
Because they are sentient beings, like my own body.
translation: I should take away the suffering of others, because it is suffering, just like my own suffering. I should help others because they are living beings, just like my own body.

academic_translation:
What are called a continuum and a collection
Are false, like a garland, an army, and so forth;
Since there is no one who possesses suffering,
Therefore, who will have control over this?
translation: A continuing stream and a collection of parts are not real in themselves. They are like a necklace or an army. Since no one truly owns suffering, who is there to control it?

Someone might ask, "Why should we stop the suffering of everyone?" There is no room to argue. If we stop it, we must stop it for all. If not, then my own suffering should not be stopped either, since I am a living being just like them.
